units.title: Present time: present simple, present continuous, present perfect simple, present perfect continuous, stative verbs
units.summary: Master all 4 present tenses and stative verbs: habits, ongoing actions, experiences, ongoing duration, and non-action verbs.

sections.title: Present Simple

forms.negative: I/you/we/they don't travel... | He/she/it doesn't travel...
forms.question: Do I/you/we/they travel...? | Does he/she/it travel...?

rules.example: Toby walks to work.

rules.use: To talk about how often things happen
rules.example: Angela doesn't visit us very often.
Carlo works in a travel agent's.
Do you have an up-to-date passport?
Poland is in the European Union.

watch_out:
We can also use do/does in present simple statements for emphasis:
• 'You don't like going by bus, do you?' 'Actually, I do like going by bus for short distances.'
• The bus isn't quicker than the train but it does stop right outside the factory.

forms.statement: I am driving... | You/we/they are driving... | He/she/it is driving...
forms.negative: I'm not driving... | You/we/they aren't driving... (or You're/we're/they're not driving...) | He/she/it isn't driving... (or He's/she's/it's not driving...)
forms.question: Am I driving...? | Are you/we/they driving...? | Is he/she/it driving...?

rules.example: Mike is driving to work at the moment.
Taxi drivers aren't stopping at the train station because of the roadworks.
Are they staying in a hotel near the Olympic stadium?
Holidays abroad are becoming increasingly popular.
Dad is always cleaning the car when I want to use it!

sections.title: Present Perfect Simple

forms.statement: I/you/we/they have flown... | He/she/it has flown...
forms.negative: I/you/we/they haven't flown... | He/she/it hasn't flown...
forms.question: Have I/you/we/they flown...? | Has he/she/it flown...?

rules.use: Situations and states that started in the past and are still true
rules.example: She's had her motorbike for over six years.

rules.use: A series of actions continuing up to now
rules.example: We've travelled by taxi, bus, plane and train - all in the last twenty-four hours!

rules.use: Completed actions at a time in the past which is not mentioned
rules.example: Have you ever flown in a helicopter?

rules.use: Completed actions where the important thing is the present result
rules.example: I've booked the coach tickets.

watch_out:
Phrases such as It's the first/second/etc time... are followed by the present perfect simple:
• It's the second time I've been on a plane.

Speakers of American English often use the past simple in situations where speakers of British English would use the present perfect simple:
• US: We already saw the Sphinx.
• UK: We've already seen the Sphinx.

Speakers of American English use gotten as the past participle of the verb 'get', except when 'get' means 'have' or 'possess'. Speakers of British English only ever use got:
• US: We've already gotten Dan a new backpack for his summer vacation.
• UK: We've already got Dan a new rucksack for his summer holiday.

sections.title: Present Perfect Continuous

forms.statement: I/you/we/they have been travelling... | He/she/it has been travelling...
forms.negative: I/you/we/they haven't been travelling... | He/she/it hasn't been travelling...
forms.question: Have I/you/we/they been travelling...? | Has he/she/it been travelling...?

rules.use: Actions continuing up to the present moment
rules.example: We have been driving for hours. Can't we have a break soon?

rules.use: Actions stopping just before the present moment
rules.example: I'm out of breath because I've been running to get here in time.

watch_out:
The present perfect continuous is often used with words and phrases like all day/week/year/etc, for, since, just, etc.:
• We've been walking for hours and I need a rest.

The present perfect continuous is not normally used with the words ever and never:
• Have you ever flown in a helicopter before? (NOT: Have you ever been flying in a helicopter before?)

Comparison: Sometimes there is very little difference in meaning:
• I have worked at the airport for four years. = I have been working at the airport for four years.
Comparison: Sometimes there is a clear difference in meaning:
• I have read that book about cruise ships. (I have finished it.)
• I have been reading that book about cruise ships. (I have not finished it.)

sections.title: Stative Verbs

forms.statement:
Stative verbs are not normally used in continuous tenses because they describe states, not actions:
• I see what you mean. (NOT: I am seeing what you mean.)

rules.example: believe, imagine, know, mean, think, understand
be, exist
hate, like, love, need, prefer, satisfy, want
hear, see, smell, sound, taste
appear, look, resemble, seem
belong to, consist of, have, include, involve, own

watch_out:
Some verbs (such as be, have, imagine, look, see, smell, taste, think) are stative with one meaning and non-stative with another meaning:
• Do you have your plane ticket with you? (state: possession)
• Are you having lunch at the moment? (action: eating)

exercises.title: Circle the correct word or phrase
exercises.instruction: Circle the correct word or phrase in each sentence.

items.text: Elizabeth usually [goes / is usually going] to bed at around eleven o'clock.
items.explanation: Habitual regular action takes Present Simple.

items.text: Dan [talks / is talking] on the other phone right now.
items.explanation: Action happening right now takes Present Continuous.

items.text: We [don't eat / aren't eating] any meat at the moment as we're both on a diet.
items.explanation: Temporary situation taking place at the moment takes Present Continuous.

items.text: [Does air travel get / Is air travel getting] increasingly safe?
items.explanation: Changing and developing situation takes Present Continuous.

items.text: My mum [calls / is calling] me every weekend without fail.
items.explanation: Regular habit (every weekend without fail) takes Present Simple.

items.text: How much [do babysitters generally earn / are babysitters generally earning]?
items.explanation: General fact/habit (generally) takes Present Simple.

items.text: [You always come / You're always coming] up with excuses for not having done your homework. It's so annoying!
items.explanation: Annoying habit with 'always' takes Present Continuous.

items.text: [I don't go / I'm not going] out much during the week but [I always try / I'm always trying] to go out somewhere on Saturday night.
options: I don't go / I always try
I'm not going / I'm always trying
I don't go / I'm always trying
I'm not going / I always try
answers: I don't go / I always try
items.answer: I don't go / I always try
items.explanation: Habits during the week and on Saturday nights take Present Simple.

items.text: No, the train [does stop / is stopping] at Cirencester on Saturdays.
items.explanation: Present simple emphatic 'does stop' for timetabled truth.

items.text: My mum [takes / is taking] part in ice-skating competitions almost every weekend.
items.explanation: Habitual regular activity (almost every weekend) takes Present Simple.

exercises.title: Rewrite correctly
exercises.instruction: Rewrite correctly. Change the words or phrases in bold.

items.text: My dad is often getting up late on Saturday mornings.
answers: My dad often gets up late on Saturday mornings.
items.explanation: Habitual action takes Present Simple: 'often gets up'.

items.text: Are you speaking any other languages apart from English?
answers: Do you speak any other languages apart from English?
items.explanation: Ability / state takes Present Simple: 'Do you speak'.

items.text: I already buy all my Christmas presents and it's only October!
items.explanation: Present result of completed action with 'already' takes Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: It's the first time I'm ever having a party at home.
items.explanation: 'It's the first time...' is followed by Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: Actually, I think Darren does works quite hard sometimes.
items.explanation: After auxiliary 'does', use bare infinitive 'work', or simply 'works'.

items.text: Carlo is never eating Chinese food before.
items.explanation: Life experience before now with 'never' takes Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: Sean already books a table for tonight.
items.explanation: Completed action with present relevance takes Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: Needs Melanie any help painting her new flat?
items.explanation: Question in Present Simple takes auxiliary 'Does Melanie need'.

exercises.title: Complete using the correct form of the verb in brackets
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct form of the verb in brackets (Present Simple, Continuous, Perfect Simple, or Perfect Continuous).

items.text: It's the first time ____________________ (I / ever / eat) octopus!
items.explanation: 'It's the first time...' takes Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: Sandy ____________________ (not / see) his sister since she went to university.
items.explanation: Action continuing from a point in time ('since') takes Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: They ____________________ (go) on holiday to Spain and won't be back until the end of the month.
items.explanation: They have gone to Spain (and are still there).

items.text: Poor Tracy! She ____________________ (write) that essay for hours now and she still hasn't finished!
items.explanation: Action ongoing for hours up to now takes Present Perfect Continuous.

items.text: ____________________ (you / ever / meet) anyone famous?
items.explanation: Question about life experience with 'ever' takes Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: ____________________ (I / try) to get in touch with Jenny all morning but I can't find her anywhere.
items.explanation: Repeated attempts ongoing throughout the morning take Present Perfect Continuous.

items.text: ____________________ (I / not finish) the book yet so I can't tell you what happens.
items.explanation: Action incomplete at present with 'yet' takes Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: ____________________ (you / already / decide) where you're going this summer?
items.explanation: Question about completed decision with 'already' takes Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: ____________________ (We / live) here for the last six years.
items.explanation: Both Present Perfect Simple and Continuous are acceptable with 'live for six years'.

items.text: ____________________ (I / never / hear) such nonsense!
items.explanation: Experience up to now with 'never' takes Present Perfect Simple.

exercises.title: Complete using the words in the box
exercises.instruction: Complete using the words in the box. Use each word once.

items.text: Have you ________________ dreamt of winning the lottery?
items.explanation: 'ever' is used in questions to mean 'at any time in your life'.

items.text: I haven't worked out how to set the timer on the video ________________.
items.explanation: 'yet' is used at the end of negative sentences.

items.text: My dad's lived in the same house ________________ he was born.
items.explanation: 'since' marks the starting point in time in the past.

items.text: The film's only been on ________________ a couple of minutes.
items.explanation: 'for' marks the duration of time.

items.text: Bruce has knocked three men out of the competition ________________ far.
items.explanation: The idiom 'so far' means 'up to the present moment'.

items.text: I ________________ get the chance to get any exercise - I'm just too busy.
items.explanation: 'rarely' is an adverb of frequency meaning 'seldom / hardly ever'.

items.text: He's only ________________ got home.
items.explanation: 'just' means 'a very short time ago'.

items.text: It's eleven o'clock and Todd ________________ hasn't come home. Where could he be?
items.explanation: 'still' expresses surprise that a situation continues.

items.text: I've never met Ruth ________________. What's she like?
items.explanation: 'before' at the end of a clause means 'at an earlier time'.

items.text: Have you finished ________________? That was quick!
items.explanation: 'already' in questions expresses surprise that something was completed sooner than expected.

exercises.title: Choose the correct answer
exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer (A, B, C, or D).

items.text: Ian ________ a shower at the moment, so could you call back in about half an hour?
items.explanation: Action happening at the moment of speaking takes Present Continuous.

items.text: ________ to Ipswich before?
options: D. Have you ever been going
items.explanation: Asking about life experience before now takes Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: I ________ to all the local newspapers and TV stations to complain.
items.explanation: Completed action with present relevance takes Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: ________ TV for the last four hours? Turn it off and get some exercise!
items.explanation: Duration of an ongoing activity (for the last four hours) takes Present Perfect Continuous.

items.text: Eric, ________ hockey competitively or just for fun?
options: D. have you usually been playing
items.explanation: Asking about general habit with 'usually' takes Present Simple.

items.text: That's the first time ________ an answer right today!
items.explanation: 'That's the first time...' is followed by Present Perfect Simple.

items.text: Jessica has ________ left, I'm afraid.
items.explanation: 'already' is placed between auxiliary 'has' and past participle 'left'.

items.text: Dan ________ in the living room while we redecorate his bedroom.
items.explanation: Temporary situation during redecoration takes Present Continuous.

items.text: Unfortunately, Simone ________ a day off very often.
items.explanation: Fact / habit with 'very often' takes Present Simple negative.

items.text: Actually, I ________ a cup of tea first thing every morning but then I switch to coffee.
items.explanation: Present Simple emphatic 'do drink' emphasizes a habitual truth.

exercises.title: Complete using the correct form of the words in the box
exercises.instruction: Complete the passage 'Ancient aviators?' using the correct form of the words in the box.
exercises.passage_text:
Everyone (1) ________ that humans have been flying for only a few hundred years. But (2) ________ it possible that ancient civilizations also had the ability and technology to fly?

In the Nazcan Desert in southern Peru, there are hundreds of lines which an ancient culture drew in the dust. On the ground, they just (3) ________ like straight lines. But when you (4) ________ them from the air, you (5) ________ exactly what they are. They are incredible and enormous pictures. The pictures (6) ________ animals, birds and symbols.

One bizarre theory, which most mainstream scientists (7) ________ with, is that the people who made the lines thousands and thousands of years ago flew above the lines in balloons. It (8) ________ incredible, but a few people (9) ________ believe it's possible.

items.text: Everyone (1) ________________ that humans have been flying for only a few hundred years.
items.explanation: Everyone takes singular present simple: 'knows'.

items.text: But (2) ________________ it possible that ancient civilizations also had the ability and technology to fly?
items.explanation: State question: 'is it possible'.

items.text: On the ground, they just (3) ________________ like straight lines.
items.explanation: Stative verb of appearance: 'look like straight lines'.

items.text: But when you (4) ________________ them from the air...
items.explanation: Verb of sense/perception: 'see them from the air'.

items.text: ...you (5) ________________ exactly what they are.
items.explanation: Stative verb of thinking: 'understand / know / see exactly what they are'.

items.text: The pictures (6) ________________ animals, birds and symbols.
items.explanation: Stative verb of composition: 'include animals, birds and symbols'.

items.text: One bizarre theory, which most mainstream scientists (7) ________________ with...
items.explanation: Opinion/belief: 'disagree with'.
Stative verb of appearance: 'seems incredible'.

items.text: ...but a few people (9) ________________ believe it's possible.
items.explanation: Emphatic auxiliary: 'do believe it's possible'.

answers: for his glasses. Have you seen them?

exercises.title: Write one word in each gap
exercises.instruction: Complete the dialogue 'Holiday Blues' by writing ONE word in each gap.
exercises.passage_text:
'You've (1) ________ looking at that timetable for the last ten minutes. It can't be that confusing!' said Sheila angrily.
'I (2) ________ wish you'd be quiet! I've (3) ________ a splitting headache thanks to you!' replied Matt.
'Mum! Dad! Please!' said Alison. 'You're both (4) ________ very silly. (5) ________ is no point at all in blaming each other. That's not going to help us find out what time the next train to Budapest is due to leave.'
'You (6) ________ quite right, darling. I (7) ________ sorry,' said Sheila.
'Me too,' mumbled Matt. 'Now, let's have another look at this timetable. Well, it (8) ________ like we (9) ________ definitely missed the last train today. That was the 18.20 we just missed, wasn't it?'
'I (10) ________ so,' said Sheila. 'I mean, it did leave at 18.20. Whether it's actually going to Budapest or not is another question.'
'Well, one thing is (11) ________ in doubt,' said Matt.
'What's that?' asked Sheila and Alison together.
'This is the worst holiday we've (12) ________ been on,' said Matt. 'Next year, we're going to try something far less adventurous.'
'Agreed!' said Sheila and Alison.

items.text: 'You've (1) ________________ looking at that timetable for the last ten minutes. It can't be that confusing!' said Sheila angrily.
items.explanation: Present perfect continuous: 'You've been looking'.

items.text: 'I (2) ________________ wish you'd be quiet!'
items.explanation: Emphatic auxiliary: 'I do wish you'd be quiet!' (or 'really').

items.text: 'I've (3) ________________ a splitting headache thanks to you!' replied Matt.
items.explanation: Have got a headache: 'I've got a splitting headache'.

items.text: 'You're both (4) ________________ very silly.'
items.explanation: Temporary behavior at the moment: 'You're both being very silly'.

items.text: '(5) ________________ is no point at all in blaming each other.'
items.explanation: Existential 'There is no point at all in blaming each other.'

items.text: 'You (6) ________________ quite right, darling.'
items.explanation: Present simple of be: 'You are quite right'.

items.text: 'I (7) ________________ sorry,' said Sheila.
items.explanation: Present simple of be: 'I am sorry'.

items.text: 'Well, it (8) ________________ like we have definitely missed the last train today.'
items.explanation: Stative appearance: 'it looks like' / 'it seems like'.

items.text: '...like we (9) ________________ definitely missed the last train today.'
items.explanation: Present perfect auxiliary: 'we have definitely missed'.
Stative verb of opinion: 'I think so'.

items.text: 'Well, one thing is (11) ________________ in doubt,' said Matt.
items.explanation: Negative expression: 'is not in doubt'.

items.text: 'This is the worst holiday we've (12) ________________ been on,' said Matt.
items.explanation: Superlative followed by present perfect with 'ever'.

exercises.title: Complete each second sentence using the word given
exercises.instruction: Complete each second sentence using the word given, so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence. Write between two and five words in each gap.

items.first_sentence: What's the price of the tickets, Jimmy?
items.explanation: 'What's the price of the tickets?' = 'How much are the tickets?' / 'How much do the tickets cost?'
'Are these your trainers?' = 'Do these trainers belong to you?'

items.first_sentence: Sasha's not keen on team sports at all.
items.explanation: 'is not keen on' = 'does not like' / 'doesn't like'.

items.first_sentence: It's only her second time in a recording studio.
items.second_sentence_suffix: in a recording studio once before.
items.explanation: 'It's only her second time...' = 'She has only been in a recording studio once before.'

items.first_sentence: We got here three hours ago.
items.explanation: 'got here three hours ago' = 'have been here for three hours'.

items.first_sentence: I started writing this hours ago and it's still not right.
items.second_sentence_suffix: hours and it's still not right.
items.explanation: Past start + still ongoing with duration = 'have been writing this for'.

items.first_sentence: This is my first experience of flying alone.
items.explanation: 'This is my first experience of flying...' = 'It is the first time I have flown alone.'

items.first_sentence: Sharon's in the bath at the moment.
items.explanation: 'is in the bath' = 'is having a bath'.

items.first_sentence: Paul enjoys surprises apart from on his birthday.
items.second_sentence_suffix: surprises, just not on his birthday!
items.explanation: Emphatic Present Simple: 'Paul does enjoy surprises'.

units.title: Travel and transport
units.summary: Key vocabulary for Travel and Transport: confusing pairs, phrasal verbs, collocations, word patterns, and derivations.

items.definitions: voyage: long journey by sea/space; journey: travelling from A to B; trip: go somewhere and return; travel: activity of travelling; excursion: short tour for pleasure.
fare: money paid for public transport; ticket: paper confirming travel; fee: payment for professional service/entrance.
live: permanent residence; stay: temporary lodging.
view: what you see from a place; sight: notable object or place that people visit.
miss: arrive too late for transport; lose: misplace and cannot find.
border: official divide between countries; edge: outermost part; line: long narrow mark.
world: planet with human society; earth: the physical globe/soil.
take: carry away from here; bring: carry toward here; go: move from one place to another.
length: measurement of size; distance: amount of space between two points.
area: part of a place/city; territory: land controlled by a state or animal.
book: reserve in advance; keep: retain in possession.
guide: show the way and explain; lead: direct movement in front of others.
season: specific time of year; period: defined stretch of time.
arrive: come to a place (arrive in/at); reach: arrive at after effort (no preposition).
native: place of birth/origin; home: place where one lives.
